# Agent systems paper library

A small, deliberately bounded reading library for studying agent
systems. Sixteen papers, seven topics, one PDF per paper stored in
exactly one place.

`papers.yaml` is the only file a human edits. Everything else that
carries a generated marker, including this README, is produced by
`scripts/build_index.py`. Notes under `topics/*/notes/` are
hand-written and are never regenerated.

## What is and is not here

Each paper is downloaded from arXiv, checked against the arXiv API,
and recorded in `MANIFEST.md` with a SHA256 and the outcome of every
check. Author lists and years come from the arXiv API rather than
being typed by hand.

There are no benchmark scores, accuracy numbers, parameter counts, or
dataset sizes anywhere in this library. Nothing is summarized on your
behalf: the note stubs are empty by design, and the one-line entries
in each topic README are reading prompts rather than descriptions of
results. If you want to know what a paper found, read the paper.

## The seven topics

- [`01-reasoning`](topics/01-reasoning/README.md) **Reasoning**. How a single call is made to produce, sample, and search over intermediate steps.
- [`02-acting-and-tools`](topics/02-acting-and-tools/README.md) **Acting and tools**. The loop that interleaves reasoning with tool calls, and where tool use comes from.
- [`03-self-correction`](topics/03-self-correction/README.md) **Self-correction**. Treating a first attempt as a draft, and critiquing it under an explicit budget.
- [`04-memory-and-retrieval`](topics/04-memory-and-retrieval/README.md) **Memory and retrieval**. Bringing outside facts into a finite context window, and managing what stays there.
- [`05-multi-agent`](topics/05-multi-agent/README.md) **Multi-agent**. Several agents, or one agent playing several roles, and the coordination that requires.
- [`06-environment-and-interface`](topics/06-environment-and-interface/README.md) **Environment and interface**. The action surface an agent is given, treated as a design variable rather than a given.
- [`07-evaluation`](topics/07-evaluation/README.md) **Evaluation**. What agent benchmarks actually measure, and what they leave out.

## Default reading path

`01-reasoning` -> `02-acting-and-tools` -> `03-self-correction` -> `04-memory-and-retrieval` -> `07-evaluation` -> `05-multi-agent` -> `06-environment-and-interface`

Multi-agent comes late on purpose: the single-agent loop should be
understood before coordination between agents is worth reading about.
Two other routes, and the caveat that all three are a study opinion
rather than a consensus, are in
[`docs/reading-paths.md`](docs/reading-paths.md).

## Adding a paper

```bash
python scripts/add_paper.py 2402.01030 \
    --topic 02-acting-and-tools \
    --tier deep \
    --builds-on 2210.03629 \
    --lab-refs 07-tool-design-aci
```

The script refuses ids already in `papers.yaml`, fetches title,
authors, and year from the arXiv API, downloads the PDF into the
topic folder, verifies it, appends the entry, creates the two note
stubs if they are absent, and reruns this index. A download that
fails verification is deleted rather than kept.

## Checking what is on disk

```bash
python scripts/verify.py --all        # re-verify every paper
python scripts/verify.py --all --offline   # skip the arXiv API
python scripts/build_index.py         # regenerate the generated files
```
